study_identification_part.si4_title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Introduce Spectral Normative Modeling (SNM) to generate efficient, high‑resolution normative ranges for cortical thickness across arbitrary regions by leveraging brain eigenmodes; benchmark against conventional approaches and demonstrate clinical utility in AD via individualized deviation maps and biomarkers.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Associations between ETVC and cognition (MMSE) evaluated via correlations: overall r = -0.45 (p < 0.0001); within AD r = -0.31 (p < 0.0001); non-significant within HC (r = -0.005, p = 0.96) and MCI (r = -0.10, p = 0.14). Group-level z-score maps contrasted HC vs AD; vertexwise associations mapped and FDR-corrected (alpha 5%).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: SNM yields fast, high‑resolution normative charts enabling individualized cortical atrophy mapping; in AD, vertex‑wise deviations and ETVC robustly relate to cognitive impairment.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: SNM achieves substantial computational gains (98.3% speedup) while matching conventional performance and providing vertex‑level normative estimates adjusted for age, sex, and site. Applied to an independent clinical cohort (HC=132, MCI=202, AD=208), SNM revealed widespread cortical thinning in AD and strong associations between ETVC and MMSE (overall r = -0.45, p < 1e-4; within AD r = -0.31, p < 1e-4), with weaker or null associations in HC and MCI. High‑resolution ETVC outperformed brain‑wide normative z-scores for predicting cognitive impairment.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Transfer learning via fine‑tuning site harmonization parameters (age/sex frozen) enables adaptation to new sites. Potential for federated learning is noted. SNM supports arbitrary spatial queries (brain‑wide to vertex‑level) and centile/z‑score outputs, facilitating individualized assessments (e.g., ETVC).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Normative distributions assume Gaussianity after covariate adjustment; lateralized (asymmetric) high‑resolution norms showed lower MSLL (reduced fit) suggesting such evaluations are less meaningful at high resolution; results are from a preprint not yet peer-reviewed.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: HCP datasets collectively N=2,473 (54.7% female), age 5–100 by HCP policy; main text elsewhere notes 5–95. Thickness in fs‑LR 32k (59,412 vertices after medial wall exclusion). Clinical MACC dataset single-site 3T Siemens Trio; processing projected to fs‑LR to enable transfer. Fine‑tuning details: age/sex frozen; site parameters tuned on 66 HC before applying to full clinical sample.
